issues.title: Instance Context can only be sourced from a Client Attestation
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
## The gap

Conveying Instance Context is welded to attestation. The mapping input in Format and Mapping is defined as exactly two things:

- a Source Instance Identity, which Conventions defines as `(iss, client_instance_id)` **established by a validated Client Attestation**; or
- an upstream Instance Context Identifier being remapped under Preservation and Authorization.

There is no third path. An authorization server that authenticated a client by some other validated instance credential cannot emit `client_instance` at all.

## Why it matters

The nearest adjacent specification is [draft-ietf-oauth-spiffe-client-auth](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-oauth-spiffe-client-auth/), a working group document that profiles RFC 7521, RFC 7523 and the same attestation base this profile targets, and that defines JWT-SVID, X.509-SVID and WIT-SVID client authentication.

A deployment using it cannot convey pairwise instance context under this profile. The practical consequence is backwards: it must stand up an attester not because it needs attestation, since SVID authentication already proves possession, but because context conveyance requires one. It pays for a component to obtain a downstream privacy feature.

Conveying context is arguably the most reusable thing this profile defines, and it is unavailable to a population likely to want it.

## Candidate fix

Generalize the mapping input to any validated instance identity, and require the consuming profile to define the continuity contract backing it. That device already exists in this document: Preservation and Authorization requires an exchange profile to define continuity and refresh binding for context derived from an input token. The same pattern would apply.

## Cost, and why this is deferred past -00

The change alters what the document is. The title and abstract describe a claims profile of attestation-based client authentication; making context conveyance mechanism-independent broadens it.

That is the severability question an earlier review already raised, suggesting context propagation could eventually be a separate specification while recommending against splitting yet. This is a second data point on that open question rather than a reason to act on it now.

Reasons to hold until the working group has seen the document:

- It is an extensibility question, not a defect. Nothing in the current text is wrong or misleading; the scope is stated and the behavior matches it.
- Deciding it unilaterally pre-empts the group on the question they would most want to weigh in on.
- It is purely additive later. A third mapping input source breaks nothing a -00 reader implemented.

## Proposed for -00

One clause in Workload and Agent Credentials noting that Instance Context under this profile is sourced from a validated Client Attestation, so a deployment authenticating with native credentials does not convey it here. That section already routes SVID authentication to the other draft and says native credentials need a separate carrier profile, but says nothing about context. Without the clause the omission reads as an oversight; with it, as a scope decision.

Then raise the generalization as an explicit open question when announcing the draft, rather than in the text.

## What would change the timing

If the SPIFFE client authentication authors ask for composability, or this is presented to the working group alongside that draft, shipping -00 with the gap costs the room. In that case make the change first and let the scope question be the opening discussion.

issues.title: Upgrade ATTESTER-ENDORSEMENT to an I-D reference once the attesters draft is submitted
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
## State today

The reference is informative, with a hand-written entry pointing at a GitHub Pages URL:

```yaml
  ATTESTER-ENDORSEMENT:
    title: "OAuth 2.0 Client Attester Endorsement"
    target: https://mcguinness.github.io/draft-mcguinness-oauth-client-attesters/draft-mcguinness-oauth-client-attesters.html
    author:
      - fullname: Karl McGuinness
    date: 2026-09-14
```

`curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-mcguinness-oauth-client-attesters/` returns 404, so the draft is not yet citable by name.

## Why it is informative rather than normative

A standards-track draft cannot normatively cite a personal editor's copy. The original change moved it to `normative:`; it was reverted for that reason.

The endorsement path is also one of two alternatives in Attester Trust. A deployment using configured attester associations never needs the other document, so informative is defensible on the merits and not only on citability.

## What to do, and when

Once the attesters draft is on the datatracker, replace the hand-written entry with `ATTESTER-ENDORSEMENT: I-D.mcguinness-oauth-client-attesters`.

Keep it under `informative:` at least until both documents are working group items. A normative reference between two individual drafts couples their advancement, and the endorsement path remains optional for conformance. Revisit if the working group wants them coupled deliberately.

## Related

This also encodes the publication order: the attesters draft goes first, this one second. That draft carries an informative reference back to this one by URL, so it gets the same upgrade in its next revision.

issues.title: Defined-term consistency: Enrollment capitalization and Receiver scope
issues.author: mcguinness
issues.body:
Two leftovers from the consolidation and review rounds. Both were identified, both were deliberately left, and both are the kind of thing a working group reviewer will flag. Tracking so they get decided rather than forgotten.

## Enrollment is defined capitalized and used lowercase

`grep -c '\bEnrollment\b'` returns 2: the definition entry and one sentence-initial use. `grep -c '\benrollment\b'` returns 25. So the only mid-sentence capitalized occurrence is the definition itself.

The document's convention is that capitalization marks a defined term. Logical Client, Attester Issuer, Source Instance Identity, Instance Context, Instance Context Identifier, Instance Context Authority, Receiver, Context Consumer and Consumer Scope are all used capitalized in running text. Enrollment breaks it.

Three ways out:

1. Leave it. The definition carries a real scoping statement, "separate from a user account, device registration, or Logical Client", and enrollment reads naturally as an ordinary noun for a record type. This is the current state.
2. Capitalize the 25 uses. Costs a rewrap pass, and "New Enrollment" reads oddly in the lifecycle table.
3. Drop the definition and fold its scoping sentence into Identifier Generation or Continuity and Lifecycle, where enrollment first matters.

## Receiver scope has no entry in Conventions

Consumer Scope is defined in Conventions. Receiver scope is not; it exists only as the Receiver Scope section heading. The two are parallel concepts and a reader meets both in normative text.

Uses now carry a pointer, either `Receiver scope ({{identifier-scope}})` in Identifier Generation and the Instance Identifier definition, or the bare phrase elsewhere. That closed the review finding but left the asymmetry.

Either add a Conventions entry for Receiver scope alongside Consumer Scope, or decide the section heading is sufficient and make the pointer usage uniform.

pulls.title: Clarify instance continuity, context interpretation, and privacy
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
## Summary

Clarify how implementations preserve instance identity during inactivity and interpret instance context after token exchange. An installation returning with the same source identity and consumer scope must recover its original mapped identifier, and a consumer must establish the instance's role before attributing a request to it in policy or audit.

- Define mapping retention, retirement, and resumption independently of attestation and token expiration.
- Preserve the distinction between a current presenter and an upstream participant through both preservation and remapping.
- Explain correlation through reused token-binding keys and require separate keys across consumer scopes when deployments require unlinkability.
- Frame shared CIMD/client identity as a deployment requirement, with a two-sentence response to per-instance `client_id` and shared `software_id`.
- Classify the endorsement specification as normative, cite ATTEST Section 4 for claims extensibility, and make the existing refresh-token key-binding limitation explicit.

Issuers using random mappings need recoverable records to support resumption. Consumer-specific identifiers alone do not guarantee unlinkability, and retaining an instance identifier does not enable use of an existing refresh token with a replacement key.

## Validation

- `make all lint`: text and HTML generation, document-name and whitespace lint passed.
- Parsed all three JSON examples and both HTTP response bodies; verified both example `cnf.jkt` values against the attestation JWK.
- Checked local cross-references, normative endorsement placement, and `git diff --check`.

pulls.title: Address end-to-end review of the 15 September editor's copy
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Applies the substantive items from the end-to-end review of the 15 September editor's copy. One commit per review item so any can be dropped independently.

| Review item | Commit | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | Frame the profile as instance sameness over time | Introduction opens with the two questions: ATTEST asks whether this is an authorized instance holding this key; this profile asks whether it is the same instance seen before. |
| 8 | State the identification-versus-authorization boundary | New Introduction paragraph: the profile establishes identity and continuity, defines no authority, and authorization profiles MAY use it as policy input. Step 3 of Request Processing now says "local instance acceptance policy". |
| 4 | Rename Instance Authority to Instance Context Authority | `iss` is defined as the authority that assigned `id`; the attester remains the authority for the underlying identity. Table and example updated. |
| 1 | Describe Instance Context as a pairwise representation | Definition and Section 7.1 state that `id` need not equal `client_instance_id` and that different issuers or consumer scopes can represent one instance by different values. |
| 6 | Define continuity by evidence | Continuity is authenticated evidence that a claimant is the same enrolled instance; key custody is the primary mechanism, not the definition. |
| 5 | Two refresh-token invariants | Identity match and ATTEST key binding are stated as independent invariants, with "instance continuity does not imply key-binding continuity". |
| 2 | Mapping stability replaces retirement | One rule: never represent one source identity and consumer scope by more than one mapped identifier. Retire/resume/restore text removed. Issuers that lose a mapping omit context; SHOULD retain while grants are live. Stated in terms the issuer can enforce, since it cannot observe attester-side enrollment retirement. |
| 3 | Provenance governs preservation | The MUST is now the provenance principle. The same-issuer default and remap-or-omit rule follow from it; "hop limit" removed; shallow preservation noted as a privacy default. |
| 7 | Scoped keys explained, not decoupled | Kept identifiers and keys scoped together, since a shared key links attestations regardless of identifier. Added the enterprise path: one configured scope spanning the Receivers, one identifier, one key. |
| 9 | Severability note | Conformance states that conveying Instance Context is optional and independent of the base profile. No split. |

Not changed: `client_instance` remains registered as a JWT claim (item 9); the reviewer did not recommend splitting yet.

Build is clean (kramdown-rfc, xml2rfc txt and html) at every commit; all anchors and references resolve.

pulls.title: Address second end-to-end review: attribution, terminology, scoping
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Applies the recommendations from the second end-to-end review of the editor's copy. One commit per item so any can be dropped independently.

| Review item | Commit | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | Require presenter binding only where context attributes a presentation | Section 7.2 no longer mandates sender constraint for every token carrying `client_instance`. A binding between presenter and instance is required only when a consumer attributes the presentation to the instance; for direct issuance, sender constraint with an instance-associated key is that binding. A bearer token with context is participation evidence only. Abstract, Introduction, conformance list, and consumer processing updated to match. |
| smaller | Type identifiers as plain strings with an octet length bound | `client_instance_id` and `id` are plain JSON strings, not StringOrURI. The length bound is 256 octets of UTF-8, a byte check rather than a Unicode scalar count. |
| smaller | Make remapping the default and preservation the exception | Issuers SHOULD remap; preservation is the MAY. |
| 4 | Separate identifier scoping from key scoping and cite ATTEST | Section 4.2 states the identifier rule and the key rule as two requirements. The key rule cites ATTEST Section 11.1 and says why this profile strengthens its RECOMMENDED to MUST across separated scopes: a shared key would leave scoped identifiers without effect. The enterprise single-scope path is retained. |
| 3 | State the ATTEST basis for instance-bound refresh tokens | Not made conditional. ATTEST Section 10.3 already binds refresh tokens to the Client Instance rather than the client, so this profile does not introduce instance-bound grants. Grant Continuity now says so with the citation and states what the profile adds: an identity that survives verified key changes and detection of a copied key with a different identity. |
| 1 | Introduce Source Instance Identity and Instance Context Identifier | Both terms defined in Conventions. Source Instance Identity is `(iss, client_instance_id)` from the attestation; Instance Context Identifier is `(iss, id)` in `client_instance`, the authority's pairwise correlator for it. Used consistently through claims, processing, grant continuity, retention, mapping, and preservation. |

Already done before this review: Instance Authority was renamed Instance Context Authority and the one-hop rule was replaced by the provenance rule in PR #2.

Build is clean (kramdown-rfc, xml2rfc txt and html) at every commit; all anchors and references resolve.

pulls.title: Editorial consolidation pass
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Editorial consolidation and compression of the body. No change to the identity model, the roles, or the protocol behavior. Appendices are untouched.

| Measure | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Markdown lines | 1039 | 908 |
| Words | 6135 | 5143 |
| Rendered text lines | 1328 | 1179 |
| MUST / MUST NOT | 54 / 18 | 47 / 13 |
| SHOULD / SHOULD NOT | 5 / 0 | 4 / 1 |
| REQUIRED / MAY | 4 / 3 | 3 / 3 |

**Consolidated**

- One identifier-comparison and opacity rule in Conventions replaces four restatements in Attester Trust, Claims, and Consumer Processing.
- Consumer Scope is now a defined term, replacing the local glosses in State and Retention.
- Mapping Stability is its own subsection under Conveying Instance Context, moved out of Attester Requirements where it did not belong.
- Instance Context and Instance Context Identifier no longer restate each other.
- Grant Continuity states the two invariants once; the separate migration MUST NOT is folded into the identity invariant.
- Access Token Binding is two paragraphs instead of three; Preservation merges the two "one instance, not a chain" statements.
- Derived-context refresh binding is a bullet in the exchange-profile list rather than a paragraph in Grant Continuity.
- Suspension is retitled Suspension and Status and is one paragraph.

**Delegated to dependencies instead of restated**

- Endorsement acceptance rules to ATTESTER-ENDORSEMENT.
- Trust withdrawal and key resolution to ATTEST Section 10.8.
- Protocol-artifact binding at redemption to ATTEST Section 10.4.
- Grant revocation semantics to RFC 6749 and RFC 7662.

**Normative requirements removed as unnecessary or scope-expanding**

- "A replacement key requires a new attestation." Inherent in ATTEST.
- "Attesters MUST NOT allow retired credentials to recreate their old identifiers." Duplicate of never-reassigned in Identifier Generation.
- "Logs MUST NOT contain raw credentials or private keys." Covered by the base security considerations.
- "An integration MUST NOT assert that a shared workload identity identifies an individual instance." Now a statement of fact pointing at continuity evidence; "integration" was not a defined role.
- "Consumers relying on granularity MUST configure it rather than parse the identifier." Covered by the global opacity rule.
- "The AS MUST enforce [artifact] binding at redemption." Delegated to ATTEST Section 10.4; this profile does not define instance-bound codes.
- "It MUST invalidate all access and refresh tokens associated with that grant." Restated what revoking a grant means.

Build is clean (kramdown-rfc, xml2rfc txt and html). All anchors and references resolve and no reference is left unused.

pulls.title: Fix pre-submission consistency findings
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Closes the findings from the pre-submission consistency read, then the findings from the review of this PR. No change to the identity model or protocol behavior.

## Round 1: pre-submission findings

| Commit | Finding | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `38c4c93`, later revised | Grant Continuity's migration exception was read as citing a section that does not define migration. | See round 2. The citation parses as a migration that establishes continuity as that section defines it, so the exception was restored. |
| `b873d38` | Artifact binding cited "either authentication mode of {{configuration}}", a section describing no modes, and cited ATTEST 10.4 although that section scopes itself to the client-authentication mode. | Name both modes inline with the ATTEST 7.6 pointer, keep the profile's own enforcement MUST, cite 10.4 only for what it recommends and where. |
| `b46213d`, `ffc6e47` | The mapping bullet cited the `id` length bound to Identifier Generation, which states none. | See round 2. Repointed at the claims section rather than deleted. |
| `4ead647` | "Correlation scope" used for two different concepts; continuity table row wording; wire-example heading; "the verifier" in the managed-device example. | Disambiguated, reworded, renamed, clarified. |
| `fc12a62` | Artifact binding shared a paragraph with two unrelated topics. | Split. |
| `8613673` | Instance Identifier was deleted as an orphan, but it had been orphaned by the earlier consolidation dropping its only use. | Definition and both uses restored. |

## Round 2: review of this PR

A review of the round 1 diff found that three of those changes were wrong or weakening. All are fixed here.

| Commit | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `4d3edf1` | Deleting the migration exception made the refresh invariant unconditional, closing an extension point while the replacement prose still implied one. The prose also claimed an attester assigns a different Instance Identifier "only for a new enrollment", which is false: identifiers are assigned per enrollment **and** per Receiver scope. | Restore the original exception. Replace the prose with one accurate sentence: this profile defines no migration procedure. |
| `4d81829` | Rewording the continuity table's first row to "process restart within an installation" made it contradict the second row at Execution granularity, where a process can be the selected unit and the two rows demand opposite outcomes. | Scope the row to Installation granularity, matching the draft's own deployment examples. |
| `0224508` | Deleting "including its length bound" left no normative constraint on the issuer's generated `id`. Only the member table's Type column and a consumer-side rejection MUST remained, so an issuer could emit an over-long `id` that every consumer must reject with no rule broken on the issuing side. | Point the bullet at the claims section, which carries the identical bound with the precise "after JSON string decoding" wording, and align the table to match. |
| `c0338d9` | "Receiver scope" appeared in a MUST configuration list at first use with no pointer; Consumer Scope was named without saying whose; the restored Instance Identifier definition omitted Receiver scope; the Source Instance Identity appositive attached to the wrong noun. | Pointers added, upstream scope named, definitions corrected. |

## Note on verification

Round 1's description claimed no requirement was added, removed, or weakened, citing an unchanged BCP 14 keyword count. That evidence was insufficient. The `id` length qualifier was removed from inside a surviving MUST bullet without changing any keyword, so neither a keyword count nor a normative-sentence diff could detect it. Constraints carried by list items under a keyword-bearing lead-in, and by table cells, need manual review.

## Gates

Lint silent, build clean, versioned -00 renders, all citations resolve, no over-long lines. The idnits items are the usual kramdown-rfc set that is not ours: the combined references wrapper, the offline status fetch for the ATTEST reference, source-map tags, and the fetched abstract of a cited draft.

pulls.title: Normative audit: demote requirements that no party can observe
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Audits every BCP 14 keyword in the body against three tests: can another party observe compliance on the wire or in a token; is it already stated by a dependency; does it have exactly one home. Eight keywords fail and are demoted to descriptive prose. No enforceable requirement is lost, because none of the demoted statements was enforceable.

| Keyword | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| MUST | 50 | 44 |
| MUST NOT | 13 | 13 |
| SHOULD | 4 | 3 |
| SHOULD NOT | 1 | 1 |
| REQUIRED | 3 | 3 |
| MAY | 3 | 2 |
| Total | 74 | 66 |

## Demoted: no party can observe compliance

These are configuration, agreement, and deployment-policy statements. Nothing on the wire or in a token reveals whether they were followed, so a conformance claim against them is untestable. Each keeps its content as a statement of the deployment model.

- Profile Selection: the client and Receiver **administratively configure** the listed items, rather than MUST configure them. A Context Consumer that requires context **configures** that requirement.
- Continuity and Lifecycle: the deployment **specifies** its evidence, freshness limits, and lifecycle boundaries.
- Suspension and Status: the recommendation that attesters and Receivers agree on short attestation lifetimes becomes a statement of what short lifetimes buy. The revocation MUST in the same paragraph is untouched.
- Attester Compromise: Receivers **limit** their attester associations and configure acceptable assurance. The prohibition on attesters overclaiming assurance is untouched.
- Privacy: the deployment MUST address other correlating claims becomes a statement that other claims and application data can correlate requests despite scoped identifiers.
- Introduction: authorization profiles **can** use instance identity as a policy input. A BCP 14 keyword in an introduction is not a requirement anyone implements.

## Demoted: already stated by a dependency

Access Token Binding restated a rejection requirement that RFC 9449 Section 7.2 already carries as its own MUST. The scoping statement that binding validation applies regardless of whether context is used for attribution is retained, since that ambiguity is one this profile creates; only the restated MUST becomes a citation.

## Considered and kept

These fail a literal reading of the observability test but are the profile's substance. An attester conformance specification that cannot say MUST about continuity verification has nothing left to say.

- **Attester Trust**, binding approved Attester Issuers to keys and clients. Configuration-shaped, but its effect is observable in accept and reject decisions, and ATTEST Section 10.8 explicitly leaves trust establishment out of scope, so nothing else states it.
- **Identifier Generation**, the entropy and derivation rules. Not verifiable from a single identifier, but they are the attester's conformance surface and the basis of the unpredictability and privacy properties. RFC 6749 states comparable entropy requirements normatively.
- **Continuity and Lifecycle**, what the attester must verify and record before retaining an identifier. This is the mechanism the profile exists to specify.
- **State and Retention**, retaining enrollment and verification records. Instrumental to continuity rather than separately observable, but without it an attester could delete its records and still claim conformance.
- **Mapping Stability** and **Grant Continuity** recording requirements. Storage-shaped, but each is the premise of an observable enforcement rule stated in the same paragraph.

## Not moved to Security Considerations

The timing side-channel SHOULD in Errors stays where it is. It hardens the non-disclosure MUST in the same sentence, and Security Considerations already points back at that section. Splitting one thought across two sections to satisfy a category serves the category, not the reader.

Lint silent, build clean, versioned -00 renders, all citations resolve, no over-long lines. The normative-sentence diff was checked against the list lead-ins and table preambles by hand, since constraints in those positions are invisible to it.

pulls.title: Reference BCP 14 in the requirements-language boilerplate
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Switches the boilerplate directive from `bcp14-tagged` to `bcp14-tagged-bcp14`, so the requirements-language paragraph cites BCP 14 as well as RFC 2119 and RFC 8174. One line.

This is the only actionable item idnits reported. It surfaced as PREFER_BCP14_REF: "Consider referencing BCP14 instead of (or in addition to) RFC2119/RFC8174, as BCP14 encompasses both specifications." The warning is gone after the change.

**Rendered result**

```
The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", ... are to be interpreted as
described in [BCP14] (RFC2119) (RFC8174) when, and only when, they
appear in all capitals, as shown here.
```

BCP 14 now appears in the normative references as a grouping entry over both RFCs. All citations still resolve, no reference is uncited, and the build is clean.

**The remaining idnits items are not ours**

Against the XML, which is the authoritative mode, five nits remain and none originates in this document:

- The references section name, because kramdown-rfc wraps the normative and informative subsections in an outer "References" section.
- A possible downref on ATTEST, whose message is "status can't be fetched"; the datatracker assigns no level to an active working-group draft.
- Four `<?line?>` processing instructions that kramdown-rfc emits for source mapping.
- Non-ASCII characters, all from generated or fetched content: a non-breaking space in the BCP 14 boilerplate, and an author organization plus two em-dashes inside the fetched abstract of a cited draft. The markdown source contains none.
- A bracketed reference inside that same fetched abstract.

Running idnits against the text output instead produces additional nits that are parser artifacts, verified individually: it reports the expiry line missing when it is present in the header, reports RFC 9068 unused when it is cited in the appendix, expects form-feed pagination that modern xml2rfc does not emit, and misclassifies an informative reference as a downref because it cannot distinguish the three references headings.

pulls.title: Mark Instance Context as attestation-sourced for native-credential deployments
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
One sentence in Workload and Agent Credentials. No normative keyword added; the keyword count stays at 66.

That section already routes direct SVID authentication to the SPIFFE working group draft and says native credentials with different `sub` or `typ` semantics need a separate carrier profile. It said nothing about context, so a reader coming from that draft could not tell whether conveying `client_instance` was available to them.

It is not: the mapping input admits only a Source Instance Identity from a validated Client Attestation, or an upstream Instance Context Identifier being remapped. The clause states that, so the omission reads as a scope decision rather than an oversight.

```
Native credentials with different `sub` or `typ` semantics require a
separate carrier profile. Instance Context is sourced only from a
validated Client Attestation ({{context-claims}}), so a deployment
authenticating with native credentials does not convey it under this
profile. {{deployment-examples}} illustrates these boundaries.
```

Whether to generalize the mapping input so this composes with the SPIFFE draft is tracked in #8, deferred past -00 because it changes what the document is and lands on the severability question an earlier review left open.

Build clean, all citations resolve, no over-long lines.

pulls.title: Readability and scanability pass
pulls.author: mcguinness
pulls.body:
Eight commits, one per finding class, from a fresh-eyes read of the rendered text plus structural metrics. No normative change: the BCP 14 keyword count stays at 66, and the normative-sentence diff shows every reworded requirement matched by its replacement.

Body grows from 5270 to 5444 words. That is the cost of orienting sentences and one new table, paid to stop readers re-reading.

## Structure

| Measure | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Top-level sections opening straight onto a subsection | 3 | 0 |
| Mapping Stability: paragraphs / longest block | 1 / 13 lines | 8 / 12 |
| Suspension and Status: paragraphs / longest block | 1 / 14 lines | 3 / 6 |
| Presenter Attribution: longest block | 15 lines | 11 |
| Preservation and Authorization: paragraphs | 8 | 11 |

Only IANA Considerations and References still open on a subsection, which is conventional.

## What changed

- **Abstract** now distinguishes what selecting the profile requires from what stays optional. A cold reader took "optional claims profile" to mean both claims were opt-in; the identifier is REQUIRED once selected, and the client picks up hard requirements.
- **Introduction** names the five roles and points at Conformance, which is where the orientation lives but not where a reader looks.
- **Conformance** becomes a table of role, what it implements, and which sections. The bullets cited no sections at all.
- **Three sections retitled.** Two were both called Errors and indistinguishable in the table of contents; they are now Attestation Errors and Context Errors. Access Token Binding is now Presenter Attribution, which is what the section is about. Anchors are explicit, so every cross-reference survives.
- **Three top-level sections** gained one orienting sentence each.
- **Definitions reordered** so no entry uses a term defined later. Instance Context Identifier was the sixth entry and used two terms the reader had not met.
- **Mapping Stability** becomes three MUSTs as bullets plus a table contrasting derived and random strategies. It was six rules in one 134-word paragraph.
- **Suspension and Status** splits into attester and Receiver duties, AS revocation, and what follows without a status channel.
- **Three passages rewritten**: the sender-constraint sentence separated subject from predicate by thirty words; the upstream-authority prohibition was a "both X and Y" of stacked possessives, now a two-item list; and one MUST was addressed to "Changes" rather than to the attester.
- **Receiver Scope** now opens with what a Receiver scope is. The definition was the last paragraph, after two paragraphs of requirements that presumed it.

## Deliberately not changed

The migration paragraph trailing Request Processing has no heading and is hard to find, but giving it one renumbers two subsections for a five-line paragraph. The key-separation MUST inside a Security Considerations bullet stays where the normative audit left it; Receiver Scope already points at it. State and Retention keeps its name, since it sits under Attester Requirements and points at Mapping Stability for the issuer side.

Lint silent, build clean, versioned -00 renders, all citations resolve, no over-long lines, idnits unchanged.
